title: Cross-region hardware noise mapping and driver sanity checks (A100 / H100 / L40S)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note that collates results from across multiple cloud regions and SKU types to characterize per-quantile latency noise (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999) and its sensitivity to driver/CUDA combinations. The goal is to move beyond coarse throughput comparisons and identify reproducible tail sources we can mitigate in the serving runtime (batching, scheduling, kernel choices, or routing logic).

Motivation / context:
- Customers report intermittent p99 spikes in production despite stable avg/p50. We suspect hardware-driver interactions and region-specific SKU firmware variants.
- Previous benches focused on steady-state throughput; this doc focuses on variance/noise patterns across percentiles and what changes when we toggle driver/CUDA combos or region images.

Experiment matrix (summary):
- SKUs: NVIDIA A100 (40GB), NVIDIA H100 (80GB), NVIDIA L40S (48GB).
- Cloud providers/regions: us-west1, us-east4, europe-west3 (different physical racks and firmware images).
- Driver versions: 525.x, 535.x, 545.x (picked because infra images in the wild vary).
- CUDA toolkits: 11.8, 12.1, 12.2 (runtime differences observed before).
- Workloads: short-infer (prompt+decode <= 64 tokens), medium-infer (<= 1024 tokens), long-context decode (4k+ prefill + decode), KV-warm vs KV-cold, streaming vs synchronous.
- Batch sizes: [1, 2, 4, 8, 16] with dynamic packing enabled in some runs.
- Controls: pinned NUMA, disabled hyperthreading, isolated background noise (no multi-tenant processes).

Measurement stack and artifacts collected:
- Per-request latency histograms at the service edge (sampling at 1ms buckets).
- GPU telemetry: sm utilization, mem utilization, running processes via nvidia-smi sampled at 200ms.
- Perf counters: kernel launch latency, pci-e request stalls (where available), DMA engine utilization via nvlink counters.
- System tracing: eBPF traces for syscalls around mmap/ioctl during kernel launches.
- Periodic thermal/power readings from node telemetry.
- Raw logs and sample requests attached to linked PR/Jira.

Representative findings (high level):
1) Quantile-shaped noise differs by SKU: L40S tends to have tighter p50-p95 but a bimodal p99 in long-context workloads. A100 shows broader p50-p95 spread under small-batch low-latency workloads. H100 shows occasional high amplitude p999 spikes that correlate with driver interrupts on some CUDA versions.
2) Driver/CUDA pairing matters: on H100, driver 525 + CUDA 12.1 produced the most frequent 20-50ms jitter spikes at p99 for short-infer; upgrading to 535 reduced frequency but introduced rare 150ms p999 outliers. Driver 545 (latest tested) reduced both frequency and magnitude on the same H100 boxes in us-east4.
3) Region image skew: identical SKU+driver combinations in different regions produced different tail shapes. We observed a single rack in europe-west3 with older vendor firmware which amplified p99 for long-context decodes by ~35% versus another rack in same region.
4) KV-cache warm state reduces median and p90 variance but does not eliminate device-level microbursts at p99 — suggests bursts are not purely algorithmic but device/driver induced (DMA draining, clock transitions).
5) NVLINK vs PCIe: on multi-GPU tests with NVLINK enabled, cross-GPU synchronization occasionally introduced 30–80ms tail spikes on A100 under certain driver versions; toggling to PCIe-only (disable nvlink when possible) flattened tail at cost of limited multi-gpu throughput.
6) Power/thermal interactions: some H100 racks show tight thermal throttling margins; when power cap reduced by 5% p50 remains stable but p99 increased, implicating DVFS transitions as a contributor to tail noise.

Numeric snapshot (example run summary, medium-infer, batch=1):
- A100 (us-west1, driver 535, cuda 11.8): p50=18ms, p90=26ms, p95=34ms, p99=76ms, p999=210ms
- H100 (us-east4, driver 525, cuda 12.1): p50=12ms, p90=20ms, p95=30ms, p99=120ms, p999=560ms (frequent 20–50ms jitter events plus occasional 400–800ms stalls)
- L40S (europe-west3, driver 535, cuda 12.2): p50=16ms, p90=24ms, p95=28ms, p99=95ms, p999=180ms (bimodal p99 cluster at ~90ms and ~220ms)

Hypotheses about root causes (prioritized):
- Driver interrupt handling + context switch paths on certain drivers generate mid-latency jitter (20-100ms) when combined with specific kernel launch patterns (many small kernels).
- DMA/PCIe link state transitions (low-power->active) cause larger p99 outliers during cold-path or sudden data movement spikes, especially on long-context > 2k tokens where KV spills occur.
- NVLINK cross-GPU synchronization in some firmware/driver combos has pathological wakeups creating tail spikes.
- Thermal/DVFS stepping on H100 in certain rack images leads to occasional micro-throttles that show up as p999 events.

Quick mitigations attempted and impact:
- Pin runtime threads + isolate CPU cores: removed some syscall-related jitter; p90 improved by ~5–10% but p99 still present.
- Pre-warm KV-cache and maintain warm workers: reduced frequency of medium p99 events but not the largest outliers.
- Switch driver 525 -> 535 on test boxes: reduced frequent jitter but introduced one-off larger outliers in some cases.
- Disable NVLINK in multi-GPU patches for suspect racks: flattened p99 but CPU overhead increased for explicit device copies.

Actionable next steps (short-term):
1) Formalize a microbenchmark that reproduces observed p99 spikes reliably (small kernels + periodic large KV spill) and smoke it across all driver+CUDA combos. Owner: Marcus. ETA: 2 weeks.
2) Run controlled power-cap and thermal sweep on H100 racks to reproduce DVFS-triggered events. Owner: Diego. ETA: 1 week.
3) Capture device-level interrupts and per-CPU interrupt distribution during p99 events (use per-CPU irqstat/eBPF). Owner: Elena. ETA: 1 week.
4) Add runtime fallback policy: if p99 for given request class exceeds threshold consistently on a region+SKU+driver combination, route to compatible variant in a different region or degrade to lower resource model (config proposal in PR #672). Owner: Aisha. ETA: prototype 3 weeks.
5) Coordinate with cloud provider support to get firmware list for racks that show outliers; request replacement or firmware updates for worst racks. Owner: infra-ops.

Open questions and things we couldn't replicate yet:
- Some p999 spikes only appeared in production under multi-tenant noise; our single-tenant isolated runs fail to trigger the largest (400–800ms) stalls. Need a controlled noisy co-tenant generator.
- Is the bimodal L40S p99 cluster due to GPU ECC recovery events? We haven't captured ECC logs aligned to request timestamps.
- Are there PCIe root-complex differences across vendors causing the region skew? Need interconnect topology maps from cloud provider.

Notes to self / reminders:
- Keep raw histograms and a snapshot of instance metadata together for each run (image id, firmware id, bios, kernel).
- Don't assume newer driver always better — empirical testing is needed per SKU and workload.
- Add a small synthetic workload that exercises nvlink memcopy paths to stress cross-GPU comms.

References / related threads:
- Slack: #infra-hw-bench link to thread INF-2187 (see linked_artifacts)
- PR: runtime change to allow per-region routing by p99 thresholds (PR #672)

Summary (one-liner):
Tail noise is real, SKU+driver+region interactions matter, and while warm caches/packing help, there remain device/firmware/driver-level sources that require a combination of runtime fallbacks, targeted driver/firmware upgrades, and better per-rack telemetry to fully mitigate.

Draft status: still collecting controlled reproductions; this doc will be iterated with more microbench outputs and an actionable runbook for infra-ops.
